newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.

text.p: Swiss shares lost steam after a firm start, giving up most of the early gains to ended slightly above Friday's closing levels.

Strong fundamentals such as favourable interest rates, a strong U.S. dollar and Friday's gains on Wall Street were not enough to offset profit-taking and a lack of follow-through buying, one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index gained 5.9 points, or 0.16 percent, to end at 3,722.7 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index rose 4.53 points, or 0.19 percent, to 2,383.98.
A one percent decline in Nestle's share price today weighed on the entire market, dealers said.

Nestle was down 15 francs to 1,402 after Friday's second half-year outlook continued to discourage some investors. Nestle reported a 20 percent rise in first-half 1996 group net profit but forecast that its profit growth rate would slow in the second half.
Also, several brokers reduced their Nestle recommendations.
Roche, Ciba and Sandoz were firmer. Roche said it and a U.S. subsidiary of Bayer signed a letter of intent to form a joint venture to market several over-the-counter drugs.
CS Holding and Swiss Re were winners among financials. CS Holding jumped two percent to 124.75.
Swiss Bank Corp rose 0.25 francs to 237.50. Industrials Alusuisse and SMH firmed.
